classification.difficultyReason: Students interpret the floor plan, establish parallel boundaries from right angles, transfer the wall angle to the table corner, and then use equal base angles and the triangle sum.

content.prompt: The following diagram is a map of the first floor of Tony’s house.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 5G question 6 floor plan above the Review exercise band
spec.description: Unshaded floor plan preserving all room labels, dividing segments, five right-angle markers, the supplied top-right 45-degree angle, the triangular shelves and the TV-table triangle with its curved identifying pointer. Ordinary source blue lines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The outer sloping wall is straight. The shelf has a marked right angle and is stated to be isosceles. The top and bottom boundaries are parallel, giving a 135-degree interior corner at the bottom of the sloping wall. The TV table is stated to be isosceles. No lengths or equal-side ticks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The source-given 45-degree angle and right-angle markers remain visible. The calculated shelf and TV-table angles are absent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Tony would like to build some wooden shelves at the end of the recreation room. Each shelf would be an isosceles triangle. Evaluate the internal angles of these shelves.

answer.worked:
The marked angle is $90^\circ$. The other two angles are equal because the shelf is an isosceles triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Each remaining angle}&=(180^\circ-90^\circ)\div2\\\text{Each remaining angle}&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
The internal angles are $90^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $45^\circ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Tony would also like to construct a TV table in the shape of an isosceles triangle. Evaluate the internal angles of the TV table.

answer.short:
$135^\circ$, $22.5^\circ$, $22.5^\circ$.

Use the parallel top and bottom boundaries to find the table’s corner angle, then use equal base angles.
answer.worked:
The top and bottom boundaries are parallel: both are perpendicular to the left boundary, using the marked right angles and the rectangular kitchen corner. The sloping outer wall is a transversal. Its co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Table corner angle}&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\text{Table corner angle}&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$
The remaining angles are equal because the table is an isosceles triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Each remaining angle}&=(180^\circ-135^\circ)\div2\\\text{Each remaining angle}&=22.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
The internal angles are $135^\circ$, $22.5^\circ$ and $22.5^\circ$.
